units.text: INT. SUPERMAN - CONTINUOUS
Now just to think that if I mentioned this episode not a soul would believe me except the people who would cut me for telling, whilst if you accused me of it nobody would believe my denial.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: taking her arms away with perfect dignity.
You are incorrigible, Jack. But you should not jest about our affection for one another. Nobody could possibly misunderstand it. YOU do not misunderstand it, I hope.
units.name: ANN

units.text: My blood interprets for me, Ann. Poor Ricky Tiky Tavy!
units.name: TANNER

units.text: looking quickly at him as if this were a new light.
Surely you are not so absurd as to be jealous of Tavy.
units.name: ANN

units.text: Jealous! Why should I be? But I don't wonder at your grip of him. I feel the coils tightening round my very self, though you are only playing with me.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: Do you think I have designs on Tavy?
units.name: ANN

units.text: I know you have.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: earnestly.
Take care, Jack. You may make Tavy very happy if you mislead him about me.
units.name: ANN

units.text: Never fear: he will not escape you.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: I wonder are you really a clever man!
units.name: ANN

units.text: Why this sudden misgiving on the subject?
units.name: TANNER

units.text: You seem to understand all the things I don't understand; but you are a perfect baby in the things I do understand.
units.name: ANN

units.text: I understand how Tavy feels for you, Ann; you may depend on that, at all events.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: And you think you understand how I feel for Tavy, don't you?
units.name: ANN

units.text: I know only too well what is going to happen to poor Tavy.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: I should laugh at you, Jack, if it were not for poor papa's death. Mind! Tavy will be very unhappy.
units.name: ANN

units.text: Yes; but he won't know it, poor devil. He is a thousand times too good for you. That's why he is going to make the mistake of his life about you.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: I think men make more mistakes by being too clever than by being too good
units.name: ANN

units.text: she sits down, with a trace of contempt for the whole male sex in the elegant carriage of her shoulders.

Oh, I know you don't care very much about Tavy. But there is always one who kisses and one who only allows the kiss. Tavy will kiss; and you will only turn the cheek. And you will throw him over if anybody better turns up.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: offended.
You have no right to say such things, Jack. They are not true, and not delicate. If you and Tavy choose to be stupid about me, that is not my fault.
units.name: ANN

units.text: remorsefully.
Forgive my brutalities, Ann. They are levelled at this wicked world, not at you.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: She looks up at him, pleased and forgiving.
He becomes cautious at once.
All the same, I wish Ramsden would come back. I never feel safe with you: there is a devilish charm--or no: not a charm, a subtle interest
units.name: TANNER

units.text: she laughs.
Just so: you know it; and you triumph in it. Openly and shamelessly triumph in it!
units.name: TANNER

units.text: What a shocking flirt you are, Jack!
units.name: ANN

units.text: A flirt!! I!!
units.name: TANNER

units.text: Yes, a flirt. You are always abusing and offending people, but you never really mean to let go your hold of them.
units.name: ANN

units.text: I will ring the bell. This conversation has already gone further than I intended.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: Ramsden and Octavius come back with Miss Ramsden, a hardheaded old maiden lady in a plain brown silk gown, with enough rings, chains and brooches to show that her plainness of dress is a matter of principle, not of poverty.
She comes into the room very determinedly: the two men, perplexed and downcast, following her.
Ann rises and goes eagerly to meet her.
Tanner retreats to the wall between the busts and pretends to study the pictures.
Ramsden goes to his table as usual; and Octavius clings to the neighborhood of Tanner.
almost pushing Ann aside as she comes to Mr. Whitefield's chair and plants herself there resolutely.
I wash my hands of the whole affair.
units.name: MISS RAMSDEN

units.text: very wretched.
I know you wish me to take Violet away, Miss Ramsden. I will.
units.name: OCTAVIUS

units.text: He turns irresolutely to the door.
No no--
units.name: RAMSDEN

units.text: What is the use of saying no, Roebuck? Octavius knows that I would not turn any truly contrite and repentant woman from your doors. But when a woman is not only wicked, but intends to go on being wicked, she and I part company.
units.name: MISS RAMSDEN

units.text: Oh, Miss Ramsden, what do you mean? What has Violet said?
units.name: ANN

units.text: Violet is certainly very obstinate. She won't leave London. I don't understand her.
units.name: RAMSDEN
